subject: chemistry-1
question: Atomic radius decreases steadily across Period 3, from sodium (Z = 11) to chlorine (Z = 17). Which explanation best accounts for this trend?

options.text: Each added electron enters a new principal energy level, so shielding grows faster than nuclear charge
Nuclear charge rises by 6 protons while electrons fill the same energy level, pulling the valence shell inward
Neutron count rises from 12 to 18, and the heavier nucleus compresses the surrounding electron cloud inward
Electron-electron repulsion falls as the 3p subshell fills, letting the outer shell relax closer to the nucleus

explanation:
Across Period 3 the added electrons all enter the n = 3 shell and shield one another poorly, while nuclear charge climbs from 11 to 17, an increase of 6 protons. Effective nuclear charge therefore rises left to right, tightening the pull on the valence electrons and shrinking the radius. Shielding grows only slightly and never outpaces the added protons, no new shell opens until Period 4, neutrons add mass but no charge and do not attract electrons, and filling the 3p subshell increases rather than decreases mutual repulsion.

ELI-10: Going across a row, you add one proton and one electron at a time, but the new electrons all land in the same outer shell rather than starting a new one farther out. Electrons in the same shell are poor at blocking each other from the nucleus, so the growing positive charge in the center is felt more and more strongly by the outer electrons. Stronger pull on electrons that are not moving farther out means the whole atom is drawn in tighter. That is why atoms get smaller as you move to the right, even though they are gaining particles.
source: OpenStax — Chemistry 2e (https://openstax.org/details/books/chemistry-2e); NIST — Reference Data / Constants (https://www.nist.gov/pml)
